meaning: Line 298 builds an uncompiled copy of the same assembly so the pre-simplification unknown list can be read at line 299, alongside the compiled system at line 301. The topology is constructed twice, so the two builds must stay in step.

could_move.what: If the assembly or element list differs between the raw and compiled builds, vars_raw no longer describes the solved system, and anything keyed off it is silently wrong.
Element ordering is fixed by sorting on name and feeds both builds; a renamed element reorders unknowns and can shift state indices downstream.
Any change to equations pushed into assembly, such as the shunt connects just above, propagates to both systems and to every m1 deck.
Fits re-enter through this constructor, so a topology change alters fitted parameters, not only plots.
Cross-model comparison decks would move on the m1 side only, so figures could change for reasons unrelated to m4/m5.

expectation: Unknown. Building the raw system is extra symbolic work and adds compile time; whether any solved trajectory changes cannot be told from this context.

check.why: Re-runs an existing fit check rather than re-fitting, so a changed unknown set or changed solution surfaces cheaply.
